brand.label: The Center Is a Lie
brand.desc: Why the candidate the party calls 'electable' is the one who loses. A data essay: the center isn't a bloc, positions barely move voters, and the establishment loses.
brand.blurb: The "move to the center to win" playbook is a lie. A data essay on who actually decides elections, and why the safe candidate is the one who loses:

zero.label: A measured zero
zero.desc: All the ads and door-knocks combined move vote choice by roughly zero.
zero.blurb: All the ads and door-knocks combined move vote choice by roughly zero. Why late-campaign persuasion is a measured zero:

trust.label: One in five
trust.desc: In 1964, three in four Americans trusted their government; today, one in five do.
trust.blurb: In 1964, three in four Americans trusted their government. Today, one in five do. Almost everything about how we vote falls out of that collapse:

window.label: The window is closed
window.desc: By the time candidates are nominated, the window to swing voters is closed.
window.blurb: By the time candidates are nominated, the window to swing voters is already closed. Why "electability" is decided before the general even starts:

risky.label: The safe one is risky
risky.desc: The safe, establishment candidate has become the risky one.
risky.blurb: The safe, establishment candidate has become the risky one. Why "electable" is the riskiest bet a party can make:

incumbency.label: Built to protect incumbency
incumbency.desc: The party is built to protect its own incumbency.
incumbency.blurb: The party is built to protect its own incumbency, which is exactly why it keeps nominating losers. A data essay on who actually wins:

1in100.label: One real centrist in 100
1in100.desc: Judged by the positions they actually hold, 46 voters in 100 look centrist but only 1 truly is. The 'moderate middle' is an averaging illusion.
1in100.blurb: The 'moderate middle' campaigns chase is an averaging illusion: 46 voters in 100 look centrist, but only 1 holds centrist positions across the board. The data:

bothends.label: Independents aren't centrists
bothends.desc: 9 in 10 independents hold at least one hard-left or hard-right position; nearly half hold both. They average to a center they don't occupy.
bothends.blurb: Independents aren't moderates in the middle. 9 in 10 hold at least one extreme position, and nearly half hold both a hard-left and a hard-right one. They only average to the center:

insideoutside.label: The middle is 6%
insideoutside.desc: Grouped by the positions they actually hold, only 6% of voters are true centrists while 75% distrust government. The winnable middle barely exists.
insideoutside.blurb: The 'winnable middle' is 6% of voters. Distrust is 75%. Group voters by what they actually believe and the center nearly vanishes while low trust swamps everything:

fundamentals.label: It's not the economy
fundamentals.desc: The worst economy in twenty years re-elected an incumbent; some of the best ones didn't. A strong economy doesn't reliably save the party in power.
fundamentals.blurb: 'It's the economy, stupid' doesn't hold up. The worst economy in twenty years re-elected an incumbent, and some of the best ones lost. What actually predicts elections:

deficit.label: The fiscal-responsibility myth
deficit.desc: By the actual record, the federal deficit explodes under Republican presidents and falls under Democratic ones. 'Fiscally conservative' doesn't track the party label.
